title: Errands
goal: Get cash and open an account, buy a SIM and top up, get your phone fixed, have clothes made, get a haircut, drop off laundry, pick up medicine and send a parcel — and ask whether something is possible or available.
intro:
Living in Kathmandu means errands: the ATM that's out of cash, the SIM shop that wants a passport copy, the phone-repair stall in New Road, the tailor who promises your kurta 'tomorrow'. This unit gives you the words and the moves for all of them.

The key grammar is the **causative** — Nepali's way of saying you *get something done* by someone else: काट्नु 'cut' → **कटाउनु** 'get (your hair) cut', गर्नु 'do' → **गराउनु** 'get done'. You already know some causatives without realising it: पढाउनु 'teach' is literally 'make read'. You'll also learn the three little verbs that every errand runs on: **पाइन्छ?** 'can you get it (here)?', **मिल्छ?** 'is it possible?' and **बन्छ** 'it'll be ready'.

vocab.note: Pronounced the English way. एटीएमबाट पैसा झिक्नु 'to take money out of the ATM'.
m. खाता खोल्नु 'to open an account'.

लाइनमा बस्नु 'to wait in the queue' (lit. sit in line), even when standing.
Also सिम कार्ड. The two networks are NTC (Nepal Telecom) and Ncell.
रिचार्ज गर्नु 'to top up'. People also say ब्यालेन्स हाल्नु 'put in balance'.
डाटा सकियो 'the data has run out'. A data bundle is a प्याक (pack).

vocab.en: to be possible, work out; to match, fit

vocab.en: to crack, break (glass, a pot); to burst

grammar.title: Getting things done: causatives
grammar.body:
English says 'I **got** my hair cut', 'I **had** a shirt made'. Nepali builds this into the verb: add **-आउनु** to the stem and the verb means 'make/have someone do it'.

**काट्नु** cut → **कटाउनु** get cut · **गर्नु** do → **गराउनु** get done · **लेख्नु** write → **लेखाउनु** have written · **धुनु** wash → **धुलाउनु** have washed · **सिउनु** sew → **सिलाउनु** have sewn · **खानु** eat → **खुवाउनु** feed.

You already know several causatives as ordinary words: **पढाउनु** 'teach' (make read), **देखाउनु** 'show' (make see), **सुनाउनु** 'tell' (make hear), **बनाउनु** 'make, fix' (from बन्नु 'be made'). They conjugate like any -आउनु verb: कटाउँछु, कटाएँ, कटाउनुभयो, कटाउनुपर्छ.

For anything without a ready-made causative, use **-न लगाउनु** 'make (someone) do': भाइ**लाई** कोठा सफा गर्न **लगाएँ** 'I made my brother clean the room'. The person made to act takes **-लाई**.

**The trap**: in casual speech Nepalis often use the plain verb anyway — म कपाल काट्न जाँदै छु 'I'm going to (get my) hair cut' — just as English says 'I'm cutting my hair'. You'll be understood either way, but कटाउनु is clearer and sounds well-spoken. With **गराउनु** the job is a word + गराउनु: **ठीक गराउनु** 'get fixed', **सफा गराउनु** 'get cleaned'.

examples.en: I'm getting my hair cut tomorrow.
I had two kurtas made at the tailor's.
We need to get the tap in the house repaired.
My sister fed the baby some rice.
Mum made me do the dishes.

grammar.title: Is it available? Is it possible? पाइन्छ, मिल्छ, बन्छ
grammar.body:
Errands run on a handful of **impersonal** verbs — verbs with no 'I' or 'you', just 'it':

**पाइन्छ** 'can be got, is available' (from पाउनु 'get'). Negative **पाइँदैन**. यहाँ सिम पाइन्छ? 'Can you get a SIM here?' · यहाँ मःम पाइँदैन 'They don't do momo here.'

**मिल्छ** 'is it possible / OK / allowed?' (lit. 'does it fit'). Negative **मिल्दैन** — the shopkeeper's polite 'no can do'. Put a **-न** verb in front for 'can one…?': कार्डले तिर्न **मिल्छ**? 'Can I pay by card?' · आजै मिल्दैन 'It can't be done today.' In the past, **मिल्यो** often means 'it fits / it worked out'.

**बन्छ** 'gets made / fixed, will be ready' — the intransitive partner of बनाउनु. The repair man **बनाउँछ** (fixes it); the phone **बन्छ** (gets fixed). भोलि बन्छ 'it'll be ready tomorrow' · बनेन 'it couldn't be fixed'. Other everyday intransitives work the same way: स्क्रिन **फुट्यो** 'the screen cracked', फोन **बिग्रियो** 'the phone broke'.

And from unit 11, **लाग्छ** for time and money: कति दिन **लाग्छ**? 'how many days does it take?', कति **पर्छ**? 'how much does it cost?'

**The trap**: don't say *म पाउँछु?* to ask if something is sold — that's 'do I get (to)?'. Ask about the thing: सिम **पाइन्छ**?

examples.en: Can you change foreign money here?
You can't get this medicine without a prescription.
Your phone will be ready the day after tomorrow.

examples.native: माफ गर्नुहोस्, दाइ, यो बनाउन मिल्दैन।
examples.roman: māph garnuhos, dāi, yo banāuna mildaina.
examples.en: Sorry, brother, this can't be fixed.
It takes a week to have a kurta made.

dialogue.title: A cracked screen in New Road
dialogue.setting: Sarah drops her phone on the stairs. Her friend Bibek takes her to a repair stall he knows in New Road, Kathmandu. Friends use तिमी; both use तपाईं with the shopkeeper.

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: के भयो, सारा? किन दिक्क लागेको?
lines.roman: ke bhayo, Sārā? kina dikka lāgeko?
lines.en: What's up, Sarah? Why so fed up?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: हेर न, मेरो फोनको स्क्रिन फुट्यो। हिजो भर्‍याङमा खस्यो।
lines.roman: hera na, mero phonko skrin phuṭyo. hijo bharyāṅmā khasyo.
lines.en: Look — my phone screen's cracked. It fell on the stairs yesterday.

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: अरे यार! न्युरोडमा मैले चिनेको एक जना दाइ हुनुहुन्छ, सस्तोमा बनाइदिनुहुन्छ।
lines.roman: are yār! Nyuroḍmā maile chineko ek janā dāi hunuhunchha, sastomā banāidinuhunchha.
lines.en: Oh man! There's a guy I know in New Road — he'll fix it cheap for you.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: दाइ, नयाँ स्क्रिन हाल्न कति पर्छ?
lines.roman: dāi, nayāṃ skrin hālna kati parchha?
lines.en: Brother, how much to put in a new screen?

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: ओरिजिनल चाहियो भने आठ हजार, कपी चाहियो भने तीन हजार।
lines.roman: orijinal chāhiyo bhane āṭh hajār, kapi chāhiyo bhane tin hajār.
lines.en: If you want an original, eight thousand; a copy, three thousand.

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: दाइ, अलि मिलाइदिनुहोस् न, मेरो साथी हो।
lines.roman: dāi, ali milāidinuhos na, mero sāthi ho.
lines.en: Come on, brother, give us a deal — she's my friend.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: ल ठीक छ, ओरिजिनल सात हजारमा गरिदिन्छु। कहिलेसम्म चाहियो?
lines.roman: la ṭhik chha, orijinal sāt hajārmā garidinchhu. kahilesamma chāhiyo?
lines.en: OK, fine, I'll do the original for seven thousand. When do you need it by?

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: आज अलि गाह्रो छ। भोलि बिहान एघार बजेसम्म बन्छ।
lines.roman: āja ali gāhro chha. bholi bihāna eghāra bajesamma banchha.
lines.en: Today's a bit difficult. It'll be ready by eleven tomorrow morning.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: हुन्छ। बिबेक, नजिकै एटीएम छ? मसँग नगद छैन।
lines.roman: hunchha. Bibek, najikai eṭiem chha? masaṃga nagad chhaina.
lines.en: OK. Bibek, is there an ATM nearby? I haven't got any cash.

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: अगाडि चोकमा छ, तर हिजो त्यही एटीएमले मेरो कार्ड खायो।
lines.roman: agāḍi chokmā chha, tara hijo tyahi eṭiemle mero kārḍ khāyo.
lines.en: There's one up at the junction — but yesterday that very ATM swallowed my card.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Seriously? So what did you do?

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: बैंक गएर फारम भरेँ, एक घण्टा लाइनमा बसेँ, बल्ल कार्ड पाएँ!
lines.roman: baiṅk gaera phāram bhareṃ, ek ghanṭā lāinmā baseṃ, balla kārḍ pāeṃ!
lines.en: I went to the bank, filled in a form, queued for an hour, and finally got it back!

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: त्यसो भए म अर्को एटीएममा जान्छु!
lines.roman: tyaso bhae ma arko eṭiemmā jānchhu!
lines.en: In that case I'm going to a different ATM!

culture:
Shopkeepers, barbers, tailors and repair men are addressed as **दाइ** (older brother) or **दिदी** (older sister) — or **भाइ / बहिनी** if they're clearly younger — never by a word like 'sir'. Be friendly and patient: errands in Nepal run on relationships, and Nepalis like Bibek will happily take you to 'their' guy, who gives a better price (**मिलाइदिनु** 'to sort out a deal' is the magic word).

Practical notes: most shops now take **QR payments** (Fonepay, eSewa, Khalti) as well as cash, but a foreign card works mainly at ATMs and bigger shops, and ATMs charge foreign cards a fee per withdrawal. A **SIM** from NTC or Ncell needs a photocopy of your passport and a photo — bring both. Tailors are swamped in the weeks before **Dashain and Tihar**, when everyone has new clothes made, so order early. Some traditional families avoid haircuts on **Tuesdays and Saturdays**, and many barbers give a free head-and-shoulder massage after the cut. 'Tomorrow' (भोलि) from a repair shop or tailor is often a hopeful estimate — ask **पक्का?** 'for sure?' and phone before you go.

lessons.title: At the bank and the ATM

tip.title: I need to…: -नु छ and -नुपर्छ
tip.body:
- **मलाई + verb-नु + छ** = 'I've got to / I need to': मलाई पैसा **झिक्नु छ**.
- **verb-नुपर्छ** = 'you have to' (a rule or necessity): फारम **भर्नुपर्छ**.
- Both use the dictionary form ending in **-नु** — not the I-form झिक्छु.

sentences.en: I need to take out some money.
I want to open a bank account.
First you have to fill in this form.

sentences.native: मलाई आज बैंक जानु छ, तिमी पनि आउँछौ?
sentences.roman: malāi āja baiṅk jānu chha, timi pani āuṃchhau?
sentences.en: I've got to go to the bank today — are you coming too?
Can foreigners open an account too?

sentences.native: लाइन धेरै लामो छ, एटीएममा जाऔँ।
sentences.roman: lāin dherai lāmo chha, eṭiemmā jāauṃ.
sentences.en: The queue's really long — let's go to the ATM.
You have to wait in the queue here.
This ATM has no money in it.

sentences.native: कार्ड हरायो भने बैंकमा फोन गर्नुपर्छ।
sentences.roman: kārḍ harāyo bhane baiṅkmā phon garnuparchha.
sentences.en: If you lose your card, you have to phone the bank.

sentences.native: एटीएमबाट एक पटकमा कति झिक्न मिल्छ?
sentences.roman: eṭiembāṭa ek paṭakmā kati jhikna milchha?
sentences.en: How much can you take out of the ATM in one go?

lessons.title: Getting a SIM and topping up

tip.title: पाइन्छ? मिल्छ? — available? possible?
tip.body:
- **पाइन्छ?** 'can you get it (here)?' — negative **पाइँदैन**.
- **मिल्छ?** 'is it possible / OK?' — negative **मिल्दैन**. With a -न verb: तिर्न **मिल्छ**? 'can I pay?'
- Ask about the thing, not yourself: सिम **पाइन्छ**? — not म पाउँछु?

sentences.en: Can I get a SIM card here?
Can foreigners get a SIM too?
Without a passport you can't get a SIM.
Is it possible to buy just data?
Sorry, it can't be done today.
My phone's run out of data.

sentences.native: तीन सय रुपैयाँको रिचार्ज गर्न मिल्छ?
sentences.roman: tin saya rupaiyāṃko richārj garna milchha?
sentences.en: Can I do a three-hundred-rupee top-up?
Can you get good tea around here?

sentences.native: नयाँ सिम चल्न कति समय लाग्छ?
sentences.roman: nayāṃ sim chalna kati samaya lāgchha?
sentences.en: How long does a new SIM take to start working?

tip.title: बनाउनु fixes, बन्नु gets fixed
tip.body:
- The repair man **बनाउँछ** 'fixes' it; the phone **बन्छ** 'gets fixed / will be ready'.
- Ask about the phone: भोलि **बन्छ**? 'will it be ready tomorrow?' · **बनेन** 'it couldn't be fixed'.
- Breakdowns work the same way, with no doer: स्क्रिन **फुट्यो**, फोन **बिग्रियो**.

sentences.en: My phone's broken — I need to get it fixed.
Will this phone be fixed by tomorrow?
My mobile fell and the screen cracked.
My phone battery runs down really fast.
Is this phone still under warranty?

sentences.native: यहाँ फोन बनाउने पसल कहाँ छ?
sentences.roman: yahāṃ phon banāune pasal kahāṃ chha?
sentences.en: Where's a phone repair shop around here?

sentences.native: दाइले मेरो फोन दस मिनेटमै बनाउनुभयो।
sentences.roman: dāile mero phon das mineṭmai banāunubhayo.
sentences.en: The guy fixed my phone in just ten minutes.
The phone couldn't be fixed — apparently I have to buy a new one.
Can you fix this watch?
Is the phone I left yesterday fixed?
When do you think my phone will be ready?
I've lost my charger — have you got one?

tip.title: Getting it done: -आउनु
tip.body:
- Stem + **-आउनु** = have someone do it: काट्नु → **कटाउनु**, गर्नु → **गराउनु**, सिउनु → **सिलाउनु**.
- You already know some: **पढाउनु** 'teach' (make read), **देखाउनु** 'show' (make see).
- No ready-made form? Use **-न लगाउनु**: मलाई काम गर्**न लगाउनुभयो** 'he made me work'.

sentences.en: I had a new shirt made at the tailor's.
My sister had a kurta made for the wedding.
How many days does it take to have a kurta made?
The tailor took my measurements.
I got the lights in the house repaired.

sentences.native: यो अलि ठूलो भयो, अलि सानो बनाइदिनुहोस्।
sentences.roman: yo ali ṭhulo bhayo, ali sāno banāidinuhos.
sentences.en: It's turned out a bit big — could you make it a bit smaller?

sentences.native: हाकिमले मलाई शनिबार पनि काम गर्न लगाउनुभयो।
sentences.roman: hākimle malāi sanibār pani kām garna lagāunubhayo.
sentences.en: My boss made me work on Saturday too.

sentences.native: उसले मलाई आफ्नो नयाँ लुगा देखायो।
sentences.roman: usle malāi āphno nayāṃ lugā dekhāyo.
sentences.en: She showed me her new clothes.

sentences.native: दर्जीले नाप लिएर भोलि आउनू भन्नुभयो।
sentences.roman: darjile nāp liera bholi āunu bhannubhayo.
sentences.en: The tailor took my measurements and said to come tomorrow.

lessons.title: A haircut, a shave and the laundry

tip.title: Cutting or getting it cut?
tip.body:
- To the barber, ask a favour with **-इदिनुहोस्**: छोटो **काटिदिनुहोस्** 'cut it short for me'.
- About yourself, use the causative: म कपाल **कटाउँछु** 'I'm getting a haircut'.
- Friends ask **कसले काट्यो?** 'who cut it?' — the barber did the cutting.

sentences.native: आज म कपाल कटाउन सैलुन जाँदै छु।
sentences.roman: āja ma kapāl kaṭāuna sailun jāṃdai chhu.
sentences.en: I'm off to the barber's to get a haircut today.
A shave too, please.

sentences.roman: yo chakki dinko kati paṭak khāne?

sentences.en: Take this prescription to the pharmacy.
